items_missed: Never asked for or used the customer's name — Ryan gave it in the first line and Cameron used 'sir' twice instead, zero name use across 14.5 minutes
No 'how are you today?' — went straight from the greeting to 'do you have a few minutes'
Agenda statement covered the right content (gather details, estimate, pricing structure, perks, expected duration) but gave no time expectation, so it does not clear the agenda-opener bar
Never asked whether they needed packing services
Missed a clear emotional cue — the customer volunteered 'I'm splitting up from my partner' and Cameron responded with 'Okay. Okay.' and moved straight to the inventory list. No acknowledgment at all
No 'pricing is super simple' opener — led instead with 'I'm gonna throw a whole lot of information at you'

Save Your Ass only half delivered: he linked organization to speed and cost and warned about loose miscellaneous items, but gave no concrete consolidation examples (toys, garden tools, loose drawer items, photos off walls), no carload tip, and no 'does that make sense' close
No equivalent used to frame the job size (school bus, apartment-worth-of-items, etc.)
Self-acknowledged talking too fast — 'speak a little fast and those liquid person'
Roughly a minute of dead air mid-call while building the quote
top_strength: Best-in-set discovery. He built a full item-by-item inventory by hand, caught that the form's '1000 sqft one bedroom' was actually a two-bedroom with a partial load, then chased the details that actually drive time — glass coffee table top comes off and gets wrapped separately, the 86-inch couch on a spiral-staircase loft with a removable railing, feet from the elevator to the door, loading docks at both ends, unit numbers at both addresses. He then named the elevator as the specific risk to his own estimate rather than hiding it, and gave both the minimum ($555) and the realistic three-hour figure ($666).
coaching_note: This was a technically excellent call undone by two human misses: he never used Ryan's name once, and he stepped straight past a customer telling him he's going through a breakup. Slow the pace down, use the name three times, and when someone hands you something like that, spend one sentence on it — the rest of his machinery is already at mastery level.
phone_presence_notes: Warm word choice throughout ('wonderful', 'awesome', 'no problem', 'I hope you have a wonderful day') but no name use, an unacknowledged emotional disclosure, and a fast info-dump delivery keep it transactional rather than connected.
audio_review_reason: Rep self-identified as speaking too fast and the transcript is heavily garbled through the entire pricing and clock block — worth an audio listen to confirm whether the customer actually received the pricing, No Worries, and Meet Your Mover content clearly, since the transcript cannot distinguish transcription error from unclear delivery.
